_readme: Our own wording (no API). {PLACEHOLDERS} are engine facts (number + unit + period/tariff); [[keys]] are engine labels (no numbers). For each field the first variant whose placeholders all exist is used. Every rendered text must pass app/llm/validator.py: run `python -m pytest tests/test_llm_v2.py` after editing.

PLAUSIBLE.unknown: a possible heating opportunity that needs confirmation

status_phrase.REPAIRED: repaired, waiting for new data to measure the saving
status_phrase.VERIFIED: a saving measured after the change
status_phrase.DISMISSED: checked by a technician with no fault found

explanation: The [[appliance]] has used more since {SINCE}, [[phrase]]. Back at its earlier level it could use about {SAVE_KWH} less over {P_WINDOW} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
action: Check that the door closes properly, then report it, because this is an equipment question for the building manager.

explanation: The [[appliance]] shows [[phrase]]: an always-on load {EXCESS_KWH} above the other flats' level over {P_WINDOW}. Depending on what can really be switched off, the potential saving is {RANGE_KWH} over {P_WINDOW}.
action: Look for devices that stay on day and night, such as chargers, routers or screens, and switch off the ones nobody needs.
question: Do you know which device is always on, and can it be switched off?

explanation: The [[appliance]] runs at {BLOCK_HOURS} even when nobody is home, [[phrase]] of potentially unnecessary consumption. If it can be switched off then, it could save about {SAVE_KWH} over {P_WINDOW} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
action: Check what is plugged in on this circuit during the day and whether it needs to run then.
question: What is this device, and can it be switched off during the day?

explanation: The [[appliance]] was on while nobody was home on {HEAT_DAYS}, [[phrase]]. Turning it down in those hours could save about {SAVE_KWH} over {P_WINDOW} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
action: Turn the heater-like appliance down when the last person leaves, and keep rooms comfortable when people are home.
question: Is this a portable heater, and is it needed when nobody is home?

explanation: The [[appliance]] usually starts in peak-price hours ({PEAK_HOURS}), [[phrase]]. Over {P_WINDOW}, starting it after the peak could have saved {SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}, for the same {MOVED_KWH} of use.
action: Next time, start it after the peak period ends instead of during it.

summary: [[Phrase]] on the [[appliance]] since {SINCE}, status [[status]] by a permutation test on day means ({P_VALUE}). Measured above the earlier level: {EXCESS_KWH} over {P_WINDOW}; a repair to that level could avoid about {SAVE_KWH} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
evidence_points: Level {OBS_RATE} after the step vs {BASE_RATE} before
suggested_check: Send a technician to check the door seal, thermostat setting and compressor of the fridge-like appliance.

summary: [[Phrase]] on the [[appliance]]: an always-on load {EXCESS_KWH} above the other flats over {P_WINDOW}. How much could be avoided depends on what can be switched off: {RANGE_KWH} over {P_WINDOW}.
evidence_points: Always-on floor above every other flat in {WEEKS_ABOVE} of {WEEKS} weeks
About {EXCESS_W} above the other flats' median floor
suggested_check: No technician needed; residents can act on this, unless they report a device they cannot control.

summary: [[Phrase]] on the [[appliance]]: it runs at {BLOCK_HOURS} also when nobody is home, potentially unnecessary consumption. If it can be switched off then, about {SAVE_KWH} could be avoided over {P_WINDOW} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
evidence_points: Level {OBS_RATE} vs other flats {BASE_RATE} at those hours
Above every other flat in each observed week, also with nobody home
suggested_check: No technician needed; ask the residents what the device is and whether it can be switched off.

summary: [[Phrase]] on the [[appliance]] since {SINCE}: used while nobody was home on {HEAT_DAYS}. Turning it down in those hours could avoid about {SAVE_KWH} over {P_WINDOW} ({SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}).
evidence_points: Heater-like use while nobody was home on {HEAT_DAYS}
Occupancy is a simulated sensor estimate; not extrapolated beyond the observed weeks because heating depends on weather
suggested_check: Check radiator function and indoor temperature with the residents before treating this as behaviour.

summary: [[Phrase]]: {RUNS_IN_PEAK} of {RUNS_TOTAL} runs of the [[appliance]] start in peak-price hours ({PEAK_HOURS}). Moving {MOVED_KWH} over {P_WINDOW} could save {SAVE_SEK_HOURLY}, with unchanged energy use.
evidence_points: {RUNS_IN_PEAK} of {RUNS_TOTAL} runs start in peak-price hours
Timing only: the cost changes only on hourly spot contracts
suggested_check: No technician needed; this is a timing habit for the residents.

headline: Your Resident Actions score: {SCORE} ({BAND}) for {P_28}
look_at: Worth a look: [[top_title_lower]] on the [[top_appliance]], [[top_phrase]]; it could save {TOP_SAVE_SEK_HOURLY} over {TOP_P_WINDOW}.
look_at_none: Worth a look: no unusual patterns were found for your flat.
action_shift: Simple action: start the [[top_appliance]] after the evening peak instead of during it.
action_report: Simple action: report the [[top_appliance]] to your building manager with one tap.
action_default: Simple action: switch off devices nobody is using before you leave.
encouragement: Small habits add up, and every check helps the whole flat.

summary: Your Resident Actions score is {SCORE} ({BAND}) for {P_28}: use {PILLAR_USE}, waste {PILLAR_WASTE}, timing {PILLAR_TIMING}. Your strongest area is [[strongest]] and the one with most room is [[weakest]].

use: Switch off devices you are not using, such as chargers, lights and screens.
waste: Make switching things off part of leaving the flat.
timing: Start the dishwasher-like appliance after the evening peak instead of during it.

headline: Portfolio of {N_FLATS} over {P_28}
bullets: Simulated potential if every finding were acted on fully: {POT_KWH} and {POT_SEK_HOURLY} over {P_ALL}; not verified.
Evidence: {N_PLAUSIBLE} findings meet their stated statistical criterion; a person still has to check them before any is treated as fact.
maintenance_note: Equipment findings for a technician check: {N_MAINT}. Behavioural findings are for residents, not maintenance.
